question: The library is a quiet place to _____ books.

The weather is cold today. You should wear a _____ coat.
Lily usually walks her dog after dinner. Today it is raining, so she is playing with him indoors. Where are Lily and her dog today?
There _____ two apples and a banana on the table.
Emma made a card for her mother. She drew a flower on the front. _____, she wrote a kind message inside.
If it _____ tomorrow, we will play soccer outside.
The museum guide spoke slowly so visitors could _____ the story.
A sign at the pool says, “Please shower before entering the water. Children under 12 must stay with an adult.” What must a 10-year-old visitor do?
option_a: Bring an adult to the pool.

question: Maya forgot her umbrella, _____ her friend shared one with her on the way home.
The class garden is open at lunch. Students may water the plants, but they must return the tools to the box before class. What should a student do after watering?
option_b: Close the garden for the day.
option_c: Put the tools back in the box.
option_d: Wait until after school to water.

question: The glass is full, so carry it _____ to avoid spilling the water.
My brother and I _____ the same bus every morning.
The new policy aims to _____ traffic in the city center.
_____ the heavy rain, the outdoor concert continued as planned.
The report provides _____ evidence that sleep affects memory.
A community garden gives neighbors a place to grow vegetables together. What is one likely benefit?
The museum is free on Sundays. _____, it can become crowded in the afternoon.
By the time we arrived, the movie _____.
The instructions were _____, so everyone knew what to do.
A school moved its start time 30 minutes later. After one term, students reported sleeping longer, but test scores were unchanged. What can be concluded?
option_a: Students reported sleeping longer, while scores stayed similar.

question: A neighborhood bookstore began hosting free reading groups. _____, more residents started visiting the shop, and several asked for a second monthly session.
The students, _____ their projects early, had time to check their work.
The instructions were brief but _____; no important step was missing.

A town added bike lanes on two busy roads. In a survey, 60 percent of respondents said they felt safer cycling there, but the town did not count bicycle trips before the change. Which claim is best supported?
option_a: Most surveyed respondents said they felt safer.
option_c: Car crashes fell on both roads.

question: The manager asked staff to _____ the cause of repeated delays before proposing a solution.
Although the new route is longer, it is _____ than the old road during rush hour.
The survey included only a small sample; _____, its results should be treated as an early signal rather than a final answer.

Riverside Library stayed open until 8 p.m. on Tuesdays for two months. Visits after 6 p.m. increased each week. The library did not collect data on total weekly visits or staffing costs. Which conclusion is supported?
option_a: Evening visits increased during the trial.
option_d: All visitors preferred the later hours.

question: The scientist urged caution, noting that the findings were still _____ and needed replication.
Had the team examined the data more closely, it _____ the error before publication.
Rather than dismiss the criticism, the author _____ it by revising the study design.
A city pilot replaced some street parking with trees and wider sidewalks. Early data showed cooler summer temperatures, while nearby shops reported mixed sales. Which conclusion is best supported?
option_b: The pilot reduced heat, but its economic effect is unclear.
option_d: The city should remove all sidewalks.

question: The app was designed to make transit information easier to access. _____, user interviews revealed that some older passengers still preferred printed maps.
The proposal, _____ several revisions, was finally approved by the committee.
The initial results are promising, but the researchers caution against drawing _____ conclusions from such a small sample.

A library extended evening hours during exam month. Visits rose, especially among students, but staff overtime costs also increased. Which follow-up would best assess whether the change should continue?
option_a: Compare learning-space use and costs over several terms.
option_b: Ask only the busiest student to decide.

question: The research team published its dataset and analysis steps so others could check the results. _____, independent groups were able to reproduce the main finding.
Rarely _____ such a detailed account of how the decision was made.
The policy was revised to address an _____ gap between the written rules and how they were applied.

A report found that a tutoring program improved average scores at three participating schools. The schools volunteered for the program, and no comparison group was included. Which conclusion is most cautious?
option_a: Scores rose at participating schools, but the program’s effect cannot be isolated.
option_b: The program caused the same gain in every school.
option_c: Students would have scored lower without tutors.
option_d: The program is effective for all students.

question: Although the prototype is faster, its performance remains _____ because it has been tested on only a few devices.
Only after the second trial _____ the team notice that one sensor had been miscalibrated.
The committee will publish the revised guidelines _____ legal review is completed.

A remote-work pilot let one department work from home two days a week. Survey responses showed higher satisfaction, but productivity data were incomplete, and employees volunteered to join. Which conclusion is most cautious?
option_a: Participating employees reported higher satisfaction, while the productivity effect is unclear.
option_b: Remote work increased productivity for every department.
option_c: Employees who did not volunteer were less satisfied.
option_d: The pilot proves that all offices should close.
